option_relations.rationale: Acute kidney injury secondary to acute tubular necrosis is a component of the broader diagnosis of Diabetic ketoacidosis complicated by acute kidney injury (acute tubular necrosis with oxalate crystal deposition) and cardiac tamponade due to pericardial effusion.

Acute kidney injury on top of chronic diabetic nephropathy is a component of the broader diagnosis of Diabetic ketoacidosis complicated by acute kidney injury (acute tubular necrosis with oxalate crystal deposition) and cardiac tamponade due to pericardial effusion, as the renal biopsy showed diffuse nodular diabetic glomerulosclerosis.

Diabetic nephropathy is a chronic condition that is part of the patient's overall renal pathology, which is further complicated by acute kidney injury as described in the more comprehensive diagnosis.
Acute Oxalate Nephropathy is a specific finding (multifocal oxalate crystal deposits) that contributes to the acute kidney injury component of the broader diagnosis.
